drift_observation.note: dev did not drift in this run: its 5 cold runs (3 probe + 2 plain) gave byte-identical text and its probe runs bit-identical per-token logit lines. Phase 1 (pilot on the dev probe build, 2 cold runs per setting, 120 tokens): L48 identical, L8 identical, Ldef identical, S192 identical, S48 identical, S8 identical; all 6 long-mode pilot runs gave one logit stream, all 6 short-mode runs another (the mirror budget alone does not change the numbers). Phase 2 then ran the fallback setting L8 (no pilot setting diverged): DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST=0 (every refill and upload from pageable memory, so on dev every one goes through the legacy-stream cudaMemcpy the commit replaces), DSV4_CUDA_EXPERT_MIRRORS=8 (in-place recycling of nearly every expert of every token-layer; 0 v4_cpu_moe lines: every decode token-layer ran on the fused GPU path) and a long first request (2041-token prompt, CPU-union prefill, decode right after it). The race is timing-dependent, so this is no evidence that dev is race-free, and this record makes no claim that cc9c9fab fixes a drift observed here. Across phases: the first 120 per-token probe lines of all 9 phase-2 probe runs (dev, H, pr0) equal those of all 6 long-mode pilot runs on dev (identical), so 9 cold dev runs of this request (6 pilot, 3 phase-2 probe) agree bit for bit on those tokens.

The speed difference is measured in a stress configuration chosen to provoke the race, not in a default one: every refill and upload pageable (DSV4_CUDA_PIN_HOST=0) and DSV4_CUDA_EXPERT_MIRRORS=8, so nearly every expert of every token-layer is refilled in place (dev decodes at 1.76 tok/s here vs 2.61 with the default budget in the pilot, P_Ldef). It says nothing about decode speed at the defaults (there the final drift run measured pr0 vs dev +0.31%, no-change).
